title: lab.common.article_tool wired into brain.reason as notes=, a hard dispatch to a genuinely different question shape
goal: Close the gap EXP-098 itself named and left open: write_article_tool existed, worked, and was schema-checked, but had no path through lab.common.brain.reason, the project's own stated single controller -- revisited on the project owner's own direct instruction rather than left as a 'maybe a sibling entry point' follow-up.
method: Three real sources (one containing a genuine 3-way payment relationship cycle) plus matching notes, passed to reason(notes=...) -- checking decision, citations, coverage, and that the cycle is surfaced, not dropped. Empty notes, checking the same abstain path (not a crash) every other malformed-input case in this module already uses. notes= omitted entirely on an ordinary lookup ask, checking that path is completely unaffected.

dependency_tree_nodes.summary: written from 3 source(s) plus caller-supplied notes

results_prose: notes= given with 3 real sources (one containing a 3-way payment cycle): decision='supported_with_flags', citations=['S1', 'S2', 'S3'], coverage=1.0, 1 relationship cycle(s) found and correctly surfaced as supported_with_flags, not silently dropped. Malformed input (empty notes): decision='inconclusive', same abstain-don't-guess path every other failure in this module already takes, not a crash or a guess. notes= omitted entirely (today's existing behavior, a plain lookup ask): decision='supported', text='30 days [P1]', zero write_article step in trace -- completely unaffected.
conclusion: lab.common.article_tool.write_article_tool is now reachable from lab.common.brain.reason (notes=, default None, zero regression for every existing caller), closing the gap brain.py's own docstring claims to close ('one controller, not a dispatcher to separate task-type engines') against a real, previously-undispatched capability. The part that matters is the dispatch is honest about the shape difference EXP-098 already identified: notes= is a hard signal on the caller's own input, not inferred from `ask`, and bypasses every ask-driven mechanism (stage planning, connector fetch, working_set, memory recall) that doesn't apply to this question shape at all, rather than forcing this capability through machinery built for a different one.
scale_down: 3 sources, 1 relationship cycle, one malformed-input case -- a proof the dispatch, citation extraction, and cycle-flagging work correctly end to end through the real reason() entry point, not a benchmark of write_article_tool's own article quality at scale (already separately measured by EXP-098).
follow_ups: check_contradiction/retrieve_budget (reason()'s own retry/cross-passage-contradiction options) are not specially guarded against notes= -- both are opt-in and off by default, and retrieve_budget's retry loop only ever fires when connector is not None, so the combination is inert today, but a caller that deliberately sets both was not tested here.

The decision label 'supported_with_flags' is reused for a relationship-cycle flag here, the same label document_write's own consistency_flags use for a different kind of flag (cross-page contradiction) -- both mean 'answered, but look closer', which is correct, but a caller inspecting trace needs to check which stage ran (write_article vs longform_write) to know which kind of flag it actually is, not just the top-level decision string.

write_article_tool's own CLI entry point (reading a JSON payload from stdin/argv) is untouched and still works standalone -- this wiring only adds a second way to reach the same function, through reason(), without removing or changing the first.
models_used: None -- write_article_tool's own pipeline (notes_to_findings, the one-finding-at-a-time deterministic splice, assemble, relationship_graph's cycle detection) is fully deterministic as of 2026-11-11 (rewriter_backends's module docstring); no model of any kind is involved in this dispatch.
